The '''2009–10 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 108th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 78th in a [[round-robin tournament]]. There were three promoted teams from the [[Serie B]], replacing the three teams that were relegated following the [[2008–09 Serie A|2008–09 season]]. [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] provided a new match ball – the T90 Ascente – for this season. Following the season, citing a larger television contract, the seventeen teams that survived the season and the three promoted sides formed a new league akin to England's [[Premier League]].<ref>[http://msn.foxsports.com/soccer/story/9986686/Italy's-Serie-A-confirms-breakaway-league Italy's Serie A confirms breakaway league] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090916051240/http://msn.foxsports.com/soccer/story/9986686/Italy%27s-Serie-A-confirms-breakaway-league |date=16 September 2009 }}, Fox Sports 26 August 2009 Retrieved 11 September 2009</ref>

The title race was only settled on the last day of the season. The title was won by [[F.C. Internazionale Milano|Internazionale]], their fifth title in a row. Inter would go on to complete the first and only [[Treble (association football)|treble]] by an Italian team by winning the [[Coppa Italia]] and [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=278289&cc=5739|title=Milito strike sets up Treble chance|date=16 May 2010|work=[[ESPNsoccernet]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=17 May 2010|archive-date=22 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622103049/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=278289&cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref>

*{{note|1|1}} Davide Ballardini was removed from his managerial duties on 5 June, contemporarily to Walter Zenga's appointment as new head coach. He successively rescinded his contract by mutual consent on 13 June.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mediagol.it/articolo.asp?idNotizia=157515 |language=it |publisher=Mediagol.it |title=BALLARDINI-PALERMO, CONTRATTO RISOLTO |access-date=16 June 2009 |date=13 June 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090616132030/http://www.mediagol.it/articolo.asp?idNotizia=157515 |archive-date=16 June 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
*{{note|2|2}} Gennaro Ruotolo had originally accepted to stay at Livorno as a permanent head coach after he guided the team to success through the Serie B promotion playoffs in June 2009. However, on 9 July the Technical Sector of the [[Italian Football Federation]] announced Ruotolo could not serve as head coach in the Serie A, as he was lacking the required UEFA Pro coaching badges. Following these events, UEFA Pro licensed coach [[Vittorio Russo]] was appointed as head coach, with Ruotolo actually serving as joint head coach to him despite appearing as assistant manager to Russo himself. He was successively removed from his assistant coaching post on 20 September.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.livornocalcio.it/notizie/notizie.php?id=4026 |language=it |publisher=AS Livorno Calcio |title=Ruotolo esonerato dall'incarico |access-date=20 October 2009 |date=20 October 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727102716/http://www.livornocalcio.it/notizie/notizie.php?id=4026 |archive-date=27 July 2011 }}</ref>
*{{note|3|3}} Siena Primavera (under-19 team) coach Marco Baroni was appointed permanent first team coach on 29 October, only to be moved back to his previous role on 23 November.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.acsiena.it/newsdetail.php3?id=8103 |language=it |publisher=AC Siena |access-date=23 November 2009 |date=23 November 2009 |title=Baroni torna alla Primavera }}{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
*{{note|4|4}} Gennaro Ruotolo was allowed to act as head coach without having the required UEFA Pro coaching badges only after having received temporary dispensation from the Italian Football Federation for a 60-day period.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Livorno/06-04-2010/ruotolo-cura-sorriso-603554789743.shtml |publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |access-date=6 April 2010 |date=6 April 2010 |title=Ruotolo e la cura del sorriso "Voglio un Livorno sfacciato"| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100408051215/http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Livorno/06-04-2010/ruotolo-cura-sorriso-603554789743.shtml| archive-date= 8 April 2010| url-status= live}}</ref>
*{{note|5|5}} Youth team coach Giorgio Melis was allowed to act as caretaker without having the required UEFA Pro coaching badges after receiving temporary dispensation from the Italian Football Federation for a 60-day period.

The list does not include [[Serse Cosmi]]'s resignation from Livorno on 24 January 2010,<ref name="cosmi_resigned">{{cite news |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/livorno/2010/01/24/news/cosmi_dimissioni_livorno-2062085/|language=it |publisher=La Repubblica |access-date=24 January 2010 |date=24 January 2010 |title=Rottura con Spinelli Cosmi si dimette| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100128200410/http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/livorno/2010/01/24/news/cosmi_dimissioni_livorno-2062085/| archive-date= 28 January 2010| url-status= live}}</ref><ref name="cosmi_resigned_2">{{cite news |url=http://www.livornocalcio.it/notizie/notizie.php?id=4293 |language=it |publisher=AS Livorno Calcio |access-date=25 January 2010 |date=24 January 2010 |title=Serse Cosmi si dimette dall'incarico di tecnico |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727103024/http://www.livornocalcio.it/notizie/notizie.php?id=4293 |archive-date=27 July 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> as it was rejected by the club two days later following a meeting between Cosmi and club chairman [[Aldo Spinelli]], with no competitive game scheduled in between the short vacancy period.<ref name="cosmi_back">{{cite news|url=http://www.livornocalcio.it/notizie/notizie.php?id=4305 |language=it |publisher=AS Livorno Calcio |access-date=26 January 2010 |date=26 January 2010 |title=Respinte le dimissioni. Cosmi resta al Livorno |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727103050/http://www.livornocalcio.it/notizie/notizie.php?id=4305 |archive-date=27 July 2011}}</ref>

== Awards ==
The 2009–10 Serie A season concluded with historical individual achievements, heavily dominated by Inter Milan after winning the continental treble. 

=== Individual Awards ===
The official awards organized by the Italian Footballers' Association (AIC) for the 2009–10 season were as follows:
